title: Upcoming IPOs, Explained Simply — September 2026
description: This week, Qualiance International Limited's SME IPO is closing, and Pranav Constructions Limited's Mainboard IPO is open. Four more Mainboard IPOs — Prasol C.

faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's ASBA (Applications Supported by Blocked Amount) facility via net banking, or through your stockbroker's platform. You'll need a demat account and a trading account.
A lot size is the minimum number of shares you must apply for in an IPO. You cannot apply for individual shares; you must apply in multiples of the specified lot.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Mainboard and an SME IPO?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger companies and list on the main exchanges (NSE/BSE). SME IPOs are for smaller companies and list on dedicated SME platforms, often with different rules and minimum investment amounts.

faq.q: What happens if I don't get an allotment?
faq.a: If you don't get an allotment, the money you had blocked for the IPO in your bank account will be unblocked and returned to you.

faq.q: Can I sell my shares immediately after allotment?
faq.a: Once the shares are listed on the stock exchange, you are free to buy or sell them just like any other stock in the secondary market.
